react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome converges overwhelmingly on arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid biosynthesis across three independent analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' as the top hit with FDR = 9.7e-14 and a fold enrichment of 1429.7, with five of nine input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2, and leukotriene A4) hitting the pathway. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently returns 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as rank 1 (p = 0.0015) with a 100% overlap (13 of 13 pathway compounds matched to input metabolites), spanning glycerol, arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA similarly places KEGG:hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism) at rank 1, populated by arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the upstream substrate from which three enzymatic branches emanate: COX/PGHS enzymes yield prostaglandins including 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2; 5-LOX generates leukotriene A4 and subsequently 5-HETE; 15-LOX produces 15-HETE. The simultaneous elevation of all five eicosanoid-branch metabolites in the treatment group indicates global activation of the arachidonic acid cascade, consistent with an inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or eicosanoid-receptor-signalling perturbation. Glycerol (C00116) links the eicosanoid signal to glycerophospholipid turnover, supported by Mummichog's rank-2 'Glycerophospholipid metabolism' hit. N-acetylgalactosamine (C01074) is resolved to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine and maps to sialic acid / N-glycan pathways without intersecting the eicosanoid core. 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109) and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156) appear as peripheral hits (valine biosynthesis, phenylalanine metabolism) and do not replicate across paradigms.

  "narrative_text": "The nine significantly different metabolites converge on eicosanoid biosynthesis and arachidonic acid metabolism across three independent analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR=9.71e-14 and five of nine input metabolites as members (15-HETE, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2, arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4). Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently returns Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top hit (p=0.0014, 13 of 13 pathway compounds matched to input) and Glycerophospholipid metabolism as the second hit (p=0.0096, 8 matched). Leukotriene metabolism ranks fourth in mummichog (p=0.036). SMPDB also returns Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00353, FDR=2.54e-13) as a significant drug-pathway entry with the same five eicosanoid members. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the driver metabolite: 5-lipoxygenase converts it to 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) and leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 15-lipoxygenase produces 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and COX/PGHS enzymes yield 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717). Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) is a substrate in Glycerophospholipid metabolism, where it contributes to membrane lipid remodelling that releases arachidonic acid. N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) does not intersect the eicosanoid core; it maps to Sialic acid metabolism (MUMM:sialic_acid_metabolism, p=0.052) via database aliasing to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. 2-ketobutyric acid (KEGG:C00109) and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (KEGG:C00156) do not replicate across paradigms.",

{
  "narrative_text": "The nine significantly different metabolites converge on eicosanoid biosynthesis and arachidonic acid metabolism across three independent analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR=9.71e-14 and five of nine input metabolites as members (15-HETE, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2, arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4). Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently returns Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top hit (p=0.0014, 13 of 13 pathway compounds matched to input) and Glycerophospholipid metabolism as the second hit (p=0.0096, 8 matched). Leukotriene metabolism ranks fourth in mummichog (p=0.036). SMPDB also returns Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00353, FDR=2.54e-13) as a significant drug-pathway entry with the same five eicosanoid members.
